title: Conflict misses
description: Two lines that share a set push each other out of a *direct-mapped* cache. A second way fixes it.

steps.text: The trace loads `0x000`, then `0x080`, then `0x000` and `0x080` again. Both addresses have index `000`, so both use set 0, which has room for one line. How many of the four loads will hit?
steps.explain: None. The first two loads bring their lines in for the first time; after that, each load pushes out the line the next one needs.
steps.hint: Set 0 holds one line. What happens to `0x000` when `0x080` arrives?

steps.text: Run the trace: press Run, or press Shift+Space four times.
steps.hint: Press Run in the transport bar. If the trace has already run, press Reset, then Run.

steps.text: The stats show four misses. The first two are *compulsory*: those lines had never been loaded. The other two are *conflict* misses: the line had been there, but another line in the same set pushed it out while the other seven sets stood empty. A cache that could put any line anywhere would have kept it.
Give the cache two ways: set Associativity to 2-way. The cache will ask to reset; choose Reset and apply.
steps.hint: Associativity is in the bar above the cache. Pick the 2-way option.
Press Run in the transport bar.

steps.text: Two misses, both compulsory, and two hits. With two ways, set 0 holds `0x000` and `0x080` together, so neither pushes the other out.
